 import uuid
 from collections import defaultdict
 from datetime import date
 from decimal import Decimal
 
 from fpdf import FPDF

 from src.backend.db.repositories.boq_repo import get_by_id as get_boq_by_id
 from src.backend.db.repositories.client_repo import get_by_id as get_client_by_id
 from src.backend.db.repositories.project_repo import get_by_id as get_project_by_id

 from src.backend.models.boq import BOQItem
 from src.backend.models.quote import Quote
 
 
 class _SWAPdf(FPDF):
     def header(self) -> None:
         self.set_font("Helvetica", "B", 12)
         self.cell(0, 8, "SWA Consultancy Pvt. Ltd.", new_x="LMARGIN", new_y="NEXT", align="C")
         self.set_draw_color(100, 100, 100)
         self.line(10, self.get_y(), 200, self.get_y())
         self.ln(4)
 
     def footer(self) -> None:
         self.set_y(-15)
         self.set_font("Helvetica", "I", 8)
         self.set_text_color(128, 128, 128)
         self.cell(0, 10, f"Page {self.page_no()}/{{nb}}", align="C")
 
     def _section_title(self, title: str) -> None:
         self.set_font("Helvetica", "B", 11)
         self.set_fill_color(230, 230, 230)
         self.cell(0, 8, title, new_x="LMARGIN", new_y="NEXT", fill=True)
         self.ln(2)
 
     def _kv_row(self, label: str, value: str, label_w: int = 50, val_w: int = 130) -> None:
         self.set_font("Helvetica", "B", 10)
         self.cell(label_w, 7, label)
         self.set_font("Helvetica", "", 10)
         self.cell(val_w, 7, value, new_x="LMARGIN", new_y="NEXT")
 
     def _table_header(self, headers: list[str], widths: list[int]) -> None:
         self.set_font("Helvetica", "B", 9)
         self.set_fill_color(200, 200, 200)
         for i, h in enumerate(headers):
             self.cell(widths[i], 7, h, border=1, fill=True, align="C")
         self.ln()
 
     def _table_row(self, values: list[str], widths: list[int], aligns: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
         self.set_font("Helvetica", "", 8)
         if aligns is None:
             aligns = ["L"] * len(values)
         for i, val in enumerate(values):
             self.cell(widths[i], 6, val, border=1, align=aligns[i])
         self.ln()
 
 
 def _safe_str(val: object | None, fallback: str = "N/A") -> str:
     if val is None:
         return fallback
     return str(val)
 
 
 def _fmt_decimal(val: Decimal | float | str | None, fallback: str = "0.00") -> str:
     if val is None:
         return fallback
     return f"{Decimal(str(val)):,.2f}"
 
 
 def _fmt_date(val: date | None, fallback: str = "N/A") -> str:
     if val is None:
         return fallback
     return val.strftime("%d %b %Y")
 
 
 def export_project_summary(db: Session, project_id: uuid.UUID) -> bytes:
     project = get_project_by_id(db, project_id)
     if not project:
         raise ValueError("Project not found")
 
     client = get_client_by_id(db, project.client_id) if project.client_id else None
     pm = get_user_by_id(db, project.pm_id) if project.pm_id else None
     designer = get_user_by_id(db, project.designer_id) if project.designer_id else None
     auditor = get_user_by_id(db, project.auditor_id) if project.auditor_id else None
 
     boq_items = (
         db.query(BOQItem)
         .join(BOQItem.boq)
         .filter(BOQItem.boq.has(project_id=project_id))
         .all()
     )
     boq_total = sum((item.amount for item in boq_items), Decimal("0"))
     boq_count = len(boq_items)
 
     task_counts = get_task_counts_by_project(db, project_id)
     tasks_total = sum(task_counts.values())
 
     team = []
     if pm:
         team.append(("Project Manager", pm.name))
     if designer:
         team.append(("Designer", designer.name))
     if auditor:
         team.append(("Auditor", auditor.name))
 
     pdf = _SWAPdf()
     pdf.alias_nb_pages()
     pdf.set_auto_page_break(auto=True, margin=15)
     pdf.add_page()
 
     pdf._section_title("Project Information")
     pdf._kv_row("Project Name:", _safe_str(project.name))
     pdf._kv_row("Project Code:", _safe_str(project.code))
     pdf._kv_row("Client:", _safe_str(client.name if client else None))
     pdf._kv_row("Status:", project.status.replace("_", " ").title())
     pdf._kv_row("Location:", _safe_str(project.location))
     pdf._kv_row("Start Date:", _fmt_date(project.start_date))
     pdf._kv_row("Target End:", _fmt_date(project.target_end_date))
     pdf._kv_row("Estimated Value:", _fmt_decimal(project.estimated_value))
     pdf._kv_row("Actual Value:", _fmt_decimal(project.actual_value))
     pdf.ln(4)
 
     pdf._section_title("BOQ Summary")
     pdf._kv_row("Total BOQ Value:", _fmt_decimal(boq_total))
     pdf._kv_row("Item Count:", str(boq_count))
     pdf.ln(4)
 
     pdf._section_title("Task Status Breakdown")
     pdf._table_header(["Status", "Count"], [60, 40])
     for status_key in ("todo", "in_progress", "done"):
         count = task_counts.get(status_key, 0)
         label = status_key.replace("_", " ").title()
         pdf._table_row([label, str(count)], [60, 40], ["L", "R"])
     pdf._table_row(["Total", str(tasks_total)], [60, 40], ["L", "R"])
     pdf.ln(4)
 
     if team:
         pdf._section_title("Team Members")
         pdf._table_header(["Role", "Name"], [60, 120])
         for role, name in team:
             pdf._table_row([role, name], [60, 120])
     pdf.ln(4)
 
     return bytes(pdf.output())
 
 
 def export_financial_report(db: Session, start_date: date, end_date: date) -> bytes:
     from datetime import timedelta
 
     time_entries, _, _, _ = list_time_entries(
         db, start_date=start_date, end_date=end_date, page=1, page_size=10000
     )
 
     monthly_hours: dict[str, Decimal] = defaultdict(Decimal)
     billable_hours: dict[str, Decimal] = defaultdict(Decimal)
     for entry in time_entries:
         month_key = entry.date.strftime("%Y-%m")
         monthly_hours[month_key] += entry.hours
         if entry.is_billable:
             billable_hours[month_key] += entry.hours
 
     quotes = db.query(Quote).filter(
         Quote.deleted_at.is_(None),
         Quote.created_at >= start_date,
         Quote.created_at <= end_date + timedelta(days=1),
     ).all()
 
     accepted = [q for q in quotes if q.client_response == "accepted"]
     pending = [q for q in quotes if q.status in ("sent", "pending_approval")]
     total_revenue = sum((q.total_amount for q in accepted), Decimal("0"))
     total_pending = sum((q.total_amount for q in pending), Decimal("0"))
 
     pdf = _SWAPdf()
     pdf.alias_nb_pages()
     pdf.set_auto_page_break(auto=True, margin=15)
     pdf.add_page()
 
     pdf._section_title("Financial Report")
     pdf._kv_row("Period:", f"{_fmt_date(start_date)} - {_fmt_date(end_date)}")
     pdf._kv_row("Generated:", _fmt_date(date.today(), fallback="Today"))
     pdf.ln(4)
 
     pdf._section_title("Time Summary")
     pdf._kv_row("Total Hours Logged:", f"{sum(monthly_hours.values()):.1f}")
     pdf._kv_row("Billable Hours:", f"{sum(billable_hours.values()):.1f}")
     pdf.ln(4)
 
     if monthly_hours:
         sorted_months = sorted(monthly_hours.keys())
         pdf._table_header(["Month", "Total Hours", "Billable Hours"], [50, 50, 50])
         for m in sorted_months:
             pdf._table_row(
                 [m, f"{monthly_hours[m]:.1f}", f"{billable_hours[m]:.1f}"],
                 [50, 50, 50],
                 ["L", "R", "R"],
             )
         pdf.ln(4)
 
     pdf._section_title("Quote Revenue")
     pdf._kv_row("Quotes Generated:", str(len(quotes)))
     pdf._kv_row("Accepted Quotes:", str(len(accepted)))
     pdf._kv_row("Pending Quotes:", str(len(pending)))
     pdf._kv_row("Total Revenue (Accepted):", _fmt_decimal(total_revenue))
     pdf._kv_row("Pending Revenue:", _fmt_decimal(total_pending))
     pdf.ln(4)
 
     net = total_revenue
     pdf._section_title("Net Profit & Loss (Estimated)")
     pdf._kv_row("Revenue:", _fmt_decimal(total_revenue))
     pdf._kv_row("Estimated Costs:", _fmt_decimal(total_revenue * Decimal("0.7")))
     pdf._kv_row("Net P&L:", _fmt_decimal(net * Decimal("0.3")))
 
     return bytes(pdf.output())

30: ## 1. Why This Is Needed
31: 
32: When you work on a project for weeks across **OpenCode CLI sessions**, you accumulate:
33: 
34: - **43+ sessions** with overlapping work, dead ends, and abandoned starts
35: - **No single source of truth** — knowledge scattered across sessions
36: - **Agent collision** — multiple agents writing the same files, using wrong configs
37: - **Session bloat** — OpenCode DB grows to 5+ GB with stale snapshots
38: - **Cannot delete sessions** without losing work → so nobody deletes them → DB keeps growing
39: - **No parallel awareness** — agents don't know what other agents are doing
40: - **No health monitoring** — experiments silently die, and nobody notices
41: 
42: **The KleenHand solution**: Ingest every session → extract handoffs → merge hierarchically via subagents → produce ONE ultimate handoff → delete all stale sessions → run deep diagnostics → continue with clean parallel-aware execution.
43:

90: ## 3. Phase 0 — Parallel Project Status Sweep
91: 
92: Before ANY cleanup, run a **parallel status sweep** to snapshot the entire project state. This gives you the full picture before you start deleting anything.
93: 
94: ### 3.1 The Master Status Dump (run ALL in parallel)
95: 
96: ```bash
97: # ===== PARALLEL STATUS SWEEP — run all at once =====
98: 
99: echo "=== GIT LOG (last 30) ===" && git log --oneline -30
100: echo "=== GIT STATUS ===" && git status --short
101: echo "=== GIT DIFF STAT ===" && git diff --stat
102: 
103: echo "=== RUNNING PROCESSES ===" && ps aux | grep python | grep -v grep
104: 
105: echo "=== OPENCODE SESSIONS ===" && opencode session list
106: 
107: echo "=== RESULT FILES (freshness) ===" && ls -lt results/*.json 2>/dev/null | head -20
108: 
109: echo "=== DISK USAGE BY AREA ===" && du -sh results/ logs/ figures/ src/ data/ 2>/dev/null
110: 
111: echo "=== TEST HEALTH ===" && python3 -m pytest tests/ -q 2>&1
112: 
113: echo "=== CANONICAL PROGRESS ===" && python3 -c "
114: import json, glob, os
115: for f in sorted(glob.glob('results/*.json')):
116:     try:
117:         d = json.load(open(f))
118:         n = len(d) if isinstance(d, list) else len(d.keys())
119:         print(f'  {os.path.basename(f)}: {n} rows')
120:     except: print(f'  {os.path.basename(f)}: ERROR reading')
121: "

131: | `opencode session list` | How many stale sessions, their titles, last activity |
132: | `ls -lt results/*.json` | Which results are fresh vs stale, last modified time |
133: | `du -sh` | Disk pressure, unexpected bloat (e.g., 5GB OpenCode DB) |
134: | `pytest` | Whether codebase is healthy BEFORE cleanup |

159: ## 4. Phase 1 — Session Cleanup
160: 
161: ### 4.1 List and categorize ALL sessions
162: 
163: ```bash
164: # Full session dump with metadata
165: sqlite3 -column -header ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db "
166: SELECT s.id,
167:        substr(s.title,1,50) as title,
168:        datetime(s.time_created/1000,'unixepoch') as created,
169:        s.agent,
170:        s.tokens_input,
171:        s.tokens_output,
172:        s.cost,
173:        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM session_message m WHERE m.session_id=s.id) as msgs
174: FROM session s
175: WHERE s.project_id = (SELECT id FROM project WHERE worktree LIKE '%<PROJECT_DIR>%')
176: ORDER BY s.time_created;
177: "
178: ```
179: 
180: ### 4.2 Categorize sessions
181: 
182: | Category | Signal | Action |
183: |---|---|---|
184: | **Empty/abandoned** | `tokens_input = 0` | Delete immediately — no handoff needed |
185: | **Subagent sessions** | agent = "general" or title starts with "Agent" | Quick handoff — they did one specific task |
186: | **Main work sessions** | High tokens_input, meaningful title | Full handoff — core project work |
187: | **Current session** | The one you're in | Keep until done, then delete self last |
188: | **Duplicates** | Same title, same date range, one has content | Keep the one with content, delete the other |
189: 
190: ### 4.3 Structured approach
191: 
192: ```bash
193: # Step 1: Get all session IDs for this project
194: PROJECT_ID=$(sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db \
195:   "SELECT id FROM project WHERE worktree LIKE '%DRO-FairML%'")
196: 
197: # Step 2: Export all non-empty sessions
198: mkdir -p /tmp/session_exports
199: sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db \
200:   "SELECT id FROM session WHERE project_id='$PROJECT_ID' AND tokens_input > 0" \
201:   | while read sid; do
202:     opencode export "$sid" > "/tmp/session_exports/${sid}.json" 2>/dev/null &
203:     # Limit to 4 parallel exports
204:     while [ "$(jobs -r | wc -l)" -ge 4 ]; do sleep 1; done
205:   done
206: wait
207: 
208: # Step 3: Delete empty sessions (0 tokens)
209: sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db \
210:   "SELECT id FROM session WHERE project_id='$PROJECT_ID' AND tokens_input = 0" \
211:   | while read sid; do
212:     opencode session delete "$sid" 2>/dev/null
213:   done
214: 
215: # Step 4: Delete processed sessions after handoffs extracted
216: opencode session delete "<sessionID>"
217: ```
218: 
219: ---
220: 
221: ## 5. Phase 2 — Handoff Extraction
222: 
223: ### 5.1 From exported JSON, extract key data per session
224: 
225: Each export has this structure:
226: ```json
227: {
228:   "info": {
229:     "id": "ses_...",
230:     "title": "...",
231:     "agent": "build",
232:     "model": {"id": "...", "providerID": "..."},
233:     "tokens": {"input": N, "output": N},
234:     "time": {"created": timestamp_ms, "updated": timestamp_ms},
235:     "summary": {"additions": N, "deletions": N, "files": N, "diffs": "..."},
236:     "cost": N
237:   },
238:   "messages": [
239:     {
240:       "info": {"role": "user", "agent": "build"},
241:       "parts": [{"type": "text", "text": "..."}]
242:     },
243:     {
244:       "info": {"role": "assistant"},
245:       "parts": [{"type": "reasoning", "text": "..."}, {"type": "text", "text": "..."}]
246:     }
247:   ]
248: }
249: ```
250: 
251: ### 5.2 Python extraction script
252: 
253: ```python
254: import json, os, glob
255: 
256: exports = glob.glob("/tmp/session_exports/*.json")
257: for fpath in sorted(exports):
258:     sid = os.path.basename(fpath).replace(".json", "")
259:     d = json.load(open(fpath))
260:     info = d["info"]
261:     msgs = d.get("messages", [])
262: 
263:     # Get first user prompt
264:     first_prompt = ""
265:     for m in msgs:
266:         if m.get("info", {}).get("role") == "user":
267:             for p in m.get("parts", []):
268:                 if p.get("type") == "text":
269:                     first_prompt = p.get("text", "")
270:                     break
271:             if first_prompt:
272:                 break
273: 
274:     # Count tool calls
275:     tool_calls = sum(1 for m in msgs for p in m.get("parts", [])
276:                      if p.get("type") in ("bash", "write", "edit", "read", "grep", "glob"))
277: 
278:     # Generate handoff file
279:     handoff = f"""# Handoff {sid[:8]}
280: ...
281: """
282:     with open(f"handoff_{sid[:8]}.md", "w") as f:
283:         f.write(handoff)
284: ```
285: 
286: ### 5.3 The handoff_XXXX.md format
287: 
288: Every handoff file must contain:
289: 
290: ```markdown
291: # Handoff XXXX
292: 
293: ## Session identity
294: - **Tool**: opencode
295: - **Session ID**: `ses_...`
296: - **Title**: Exact session title
297: - **Agent**: build | general | plan
298: - **Model**: model ID used
299: - **Created**: date
300: - **Updated**: last active
301: - **Tokens**: X in / Y out
302: - **Messages**: N | **Tool calls**: M
303: - **Cost**: $
304: 
305: ## What this session worked on
306: [The FULL first user prompt — this is the task that was given]
307: 
308: ## What was accomplished
309: [Specific deliverables: files edited, results produced, commits made]
310: 
311: ## Current state left behind
312: - Running processes (PIDs)
313: - Uncommitted changes
314: - Known issues or blockers
315: 
316: ## Key files touched
317: [Every file this session edited or created — full paths]
318: 
319: ## Handoff evidence
320: - Last commit hash:
321: - Test status (if applicable):
322: - Results files:
323: - Config parameters used:
324: ```
325: 
326: ---
327: 
328: ## 6. Phase 3 — Hierarchical Merge
329: 
330: ### 6.1 The 3-Level Merge Architecture
331: 
332: ```
333: Level 1 (L1): Batch merge — 4-5 handoffs → 1 merged_BATCH file
334: Level 2 (L2): Intermediate merge — 2-3 BATCH files → 1 merged_L2 file
335: Level 3 (L3): ULTIMATE merge — 2 L2 files → ULTIMATE_HANDOFF.md
336: 
337: Why 3 levels?
338: - Each L1 subagent handles 4-5 handoffs → context window is comfortable
339: - Each L2 subagent handles broader themes → cross-batch patterns emerge
340: - L3 merges the two L2s → final document is exhaustive
341: - If you merge 29 handoffs in one shot → context blows up, details lost
342: ```
343: 
344: ### 6.2 Level 1: Batch (4-5 handoffs each)
345: 
346: ```
347: BATCH 1: handoff_0000 + 0001 + 0002 + 0003 + 0004
348: BATCH 2: handoff_0005 + 0006 + 0007 + 0008 + 0009
349: BATCH 3: handoff_0010 + 0011 + 0012 + 0013 + 0014
350: BATCH 4: handoff_0015 + 0016 + 0017 + 0018 + 0019
351: BATCH 5: handoff_0020 + 0021 + A_experiments + B_code + C_analysis
352: BATCH 6: handoff_D_docs + A2 + C2 + D2
353: ```
354: 
355: ### 6.3 Level 2: Intermediate (2-3 batches each)
356: 
357: ```
358: L2A: BATCH 1 + 2 + 3  (session exports — the historical record)
359: L2B: BATCH 4 + 5 + 6  (agent handoffs + final status)
360: ```
361: 
362: ### 6.4 Level 3: ULTIMATE
363: 
364: ```
365: ULTIMATE: L2A + L2B
366: ```
367: 
368: ### 6.5 Typical output sizes (from DRO-FairML)
369: 
370: | Merge Level | Input | Output Lines | Compression |
371: |---|---|---|---|
372: | Level 1 (×6) | 5 handoffs each | 150-550 lines | 1.0× (all data) |
373: | Level 2 (×2) | 3 batches each | 1000-1250 lines | 1.0× (all data) |
374: | Level 3 (×1) | 2 L2s | 2900+ lines | 1.0×+ (all data + structure) |
375: 
376: ### 6.6 Patch-based merge for huge projects
377: 
378: If you have 100+ handoffs (not 29), use patch-based merging:
379: 
380: ```bash
381: # Instead of one big merge, do parallel sub-batches
382: # Sub-batch A: handoff_0000-0019 → merged_SA.md
383: # Sub-batch B: handoff_0020-0039 → merged_SB.md
384: # Sub-batch C: handoff_0040-0059 → merged_SC.md
385: # Sub-batch D: handoff_0060-0079 → merged_SD.md
386: # Sub-batch E: handoff_0080-0099 → merged_SE.md
387: 
388: # Then L2: SA+SB+SC → merged_L2A.md, SD+SE → merged_L2B.md
389: # Then L3: L2A+L2B → ULTIMATE_HANDOFF.md
390: ```
391: 
392: This scales linearly. For 200 handoffs: 40 L1 merges → 8 L2 merges → 3 L3 merges → 1 final.
393: 
394: ---
395: 
396: ## 7. Phase 4 — Project Completion
397: 
398: ### 7.1 Identify running experiments
399: 
400: ```bash
401: ps aux | grep python | grep -v grep
402: 
403: # For each process, check:
404: # - PID
405: # - How long has it been running? (ELAPSED column in ps)
406: # - Is it making progress? (check output file timestamps)
407: # - Is it detached? (TTY=?? means survives session death)
408: ```
409: 
410: ### 7.2 Create FINAL_SPEC.md
411: 
412: Every FINAL_SPEC.md must have:
413: 
414: ```markdown
415: # FINAL_SPEC — <Project Name>
416: 
417: ## §0. CURRENT STATE
418: - Running PIDs, progress %, ETA
419: - Data completeness (X/N rows per dataset)
420: - Test status
421: - Code freeze status
422: - Blocked items

424: ## §1. IMMEDIATE — DO NOT TOUCH
425: - Which processes are running and must not be interrupted
426: - Which files are being written
427: 
428: ## §2. AFTER EXPERIMENTS — EXACT COMMAND SEQUENCE
429: - Step-by-step commands to regenerate everything
430: - Order matters (analysis → figures → PDFs → commit)
431: 
432: ## §3. STALE CONTENT TO FIX
433: - Report/paper tables that need updating
434: - Hardcoded numbers vs auto-generated includes
435: 
436: ## §4. BLOCKED ITEMS
437: - What's blocked, why, unblock strategy
438: 
439: ## §5. FINAL DELIVERABLES CHECKLIST
440: - [ ] checkpoint items with row counts
441: 
442: ## §6. COMMIT STRATEGY
443: - Which files to commit when, exact git commands
444: 
445: ## §7. NARRATIVE SUMMARY
446: - One-paragraph for stakeholders (what was found, what's done, what's remaining)
447: ```
448: 
449: ### 7.3 Run everything that can run NOW
450: 
451: ```bash

453: python3 experiments/compute_canonical_wilcoxon.py
454: python3 experiments/analyze_tau1.py
455: python3 experiments/generate_report_tables.py

463: 
464: # Tests
465: python3 -m pytest tests/ -q
466: ```
467: 
468: ### 7.4 Ensure process durability
469: 
470: ```bash
471: # Check TTY column — ?? means daemon, s000 means terminal-attached
472: ps -o pid,tty,command -p <PID>
473: 
474: # If attached (TTY=s000 or similar), restart with nohup:
475: kill <PID>
476: nohup python3 -u experiments/run_canonical.py > logs/canonical_resume.log 2>&1 &
477:

498: ## 8. Phase 5 — Agent Re-alignment Timeline
499: 
500: ### 8.1 The Problem
501: 
502: - **Agent A** used `K_inner=5` while **Agent B** used `K_inner=10` → results contaminated
503: - **Agent C** wrote to same JSON as **Agent A** → file lock contention → results frozen at 109/270
504: - **Agent D** referenced tau=100 data while everyone else moved to tau=1 → report stale
505: - **No provenance** on result rows → cannot tell which config produced which row
506: 
507: ### 8.2 The Fix: Coordination Protocol
508: 
509: This protocol is **mandatory** for any multi-agent project. Print it, paste it, enforce it.
510: 
511: ```
512: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
513: │              COORDINATION PROTOCOL (NON-NEGOTIABLE)          │
514: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
515: │                                                              │
516: │  RULE 1: ONE agent launches ALL experiments.                 │
517: │          Others NEVER run anything remotely train-like.      │
518: │          "Agent A" is the sole runner.                       │
519: │                                                              │
520: │  RULE 2: ONE writer per results file.                       │
521: │          Before launch: `ps aux | grep <filename>`           │
522: │          If a writer exists, DO NOT start another.           │
523: │                                                              │
524: │  RULE 3: Kill by PID only.                                  │
525: │          `pkill python` nukes EVERY agent.                   │
526: │          Use: `kill <PID>` or `kill -9 <PID>`                │

529: │          Mandatory provenance: k_inner, tau, radii_mode,     │
530: │          lambda_init, coordinated, pgd_steps, n_seeds,       │
531: │          epochs, dataset, alpha, seed, attack, method.       │
532: │          A row without provenance is USELESS.                │
533: │                                                              │
534: │  RULE 5: Exclusive file ownership.                          │
535: │          A = experiments/* results/* logs/*                  │
536: │          B = src/* (code + theory)                           │
537: │          C = figures/* results/*.csv analysis scripts        │
538: │          D = report/* paper/* docs/* top-level *.md          │

541: │                                                              │

543: │          Agent B finishes all code changes.                  │

547: │                                                              │
548: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

641: ## 9. Phase 6 — Deep Diagnostics & Self-Healing
642: 
643: ### 9.1 Experiment Health Check
644: 
645: ```bash
646: # Check ALL running processes
647: echo "=== ALL PYTHON PROCESSES ==="
648: ps aux | grep python | grep -v grep | awk '{printf "PID=%s CPU=%s%% MEM=%s%% ELAPSED=%s CMD=%s\n", $2, $3, $4, $10, $11}'
649: 
650: # Check process age
651: echo "=== PROCESS DURATION ==="
652: ps -eo pid,etime,args | grep python | grep -v grep
653: 
654: # Check if output files are being updated
655: echo "=== FILE FRESHNESS (last 5 min) ==="
656: find results/ -name "*.json" -newer results/ -mmin -5 2>/dev/null | head -10
657: 
658: # Check for stale (no update in 1hr) result files
659: echo "=== STALE FILES (no update >1hr) ==="
660: find results/ -name "*.json" -mmin +60 2>/dev/null | head -10
661: ```

663: ### 9.2 Disk Pressure Diagnostics
664: 
665: ```bash
666: echo "=== OPENCODE DB SIZE ==="
667: du -sh ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db
668: du -sh ~/.local/share/opencode/
669: 
670: echo "=== PROJECT DISK USAGE ==="
671: du -sh . --exclude=.git
672:

674: du -sh ~/Library/Caches/ 2>/dev/null
675: du -sh ~/.cache/ 2>/dev/null

678: ### 9.3 Common Failure Patterns & Self-Heal
679: 
680: | Pattern | Detection | Self-Heal |
681: |---|---|---|
682: | **Process hung** | CPU=0%, no file update >30min | `kill -9 <PID>` → restart with nohup |
683: | **JSON corruption** | JSON parse error in results file | Script should catch+skip bad entries, or restore from backup |
684: | **Out of disk** | `df -h` shows >90% | Find+delete caches, old snapshots, unused results |
685: | **Process killed by OOM** | Log ends with "Killed" or no error | Reduce memory (batch size, smaller model), or add swap |
686: | **Results file locked** | `write` tool fails | Kill other processes writing same file, restart single writer |
687: | **Session timeout** | Process dies when tool session ends | Use `nohup` + `??` TTY daemon |
688: | **Mixed configs** | Rows in same JSON have different `k_inner` | Add provenance field, filter by config for analysis |
689: | **Dependency drift** | ImportError after agent adds package | Use `requirements.txt`, freeze before canonical |
690: 
691: ### 9.4 Self-Healing Commands
692: 
693: ```bash
694: # Heal a hung process
695: kill -9 <PID> 2>/dev/null
696: nohup python3 -u experiments/run_canonical.py > logs/canonical_resume.log 2>&1 &
697: disown
698: 
699: # Heal a corrupted JSON
700: python3 -c "
701: import json
702: try:
703:     d = json.load(open('results/canonical_tau1.json'))
704:     print(f'OK: {len(d)} rows')
705: except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
706:     print(f'CORRUPTED at {e.pos}')
707:     # The last write was partial — truncate to last valid entry
708:     with open('results/canonical_tau1.json') as f:
709:         content = f.read()
710:     # Find last complete JSON object/array
711:     last_brace = content.rfind(']}')
712:     if last_brace > 0:
713:         content = content[:last_brace+2]
714:         with open('results/canonical_tau1.json', 'w') as f:
715:             f.write(content)
716:         d = json.load(open('results/canonical_tau1.json'))
717:         print(f'HEALED: {len(d)} rows')
718: "
719: 
720: # Heal orphaned lock files
721: find . -name "*.lock" -delete
722: find . -name "*.LCK" -delete
723: 
724: # Heal stale PID references
725: ps aux | grep defunct | grep -v grep  # Zombie processes
726: ```

1052: ## 14. Lessons Learned from DRO-FairML
1053: 
1054: ### What Went Wrong (so you don't repeat it)
1055: 
1056: | Problem | Impact | How Detected | Fix |
1057: |---|---|---|---|
1058: | **No coordination protocol** | 4 agents wrote same JSON → file frozen at 109/270 | `ls -lt` showed file unchanged for days | MASTER_PLAN §1 protocol |
1059: | **K_inner=5 vs K_inner=10** | Results silently wrong for weeks | Brute-force audit found 18 bugs | Every row MUST record its config |
1060: | **tau=100 vs tau=1** | "DRO is fragile" was actually tau artifact | Tau ablation sweep showed tau=1 fixes everything | Always sweep before concluding |
1061: | **Oracle leak** | DRO knew real corruption rates | Code review: `corrupt_mask` passed to DRO | DRO knows only α, not mask |
1062: | **pkill python** | Killed ALL 4 agents at once | All processes died simultaneously | Kill by PID only |
1063: | **No background durability** | 270-run re-run died 8 times (timeouts, Terminated:15) | Logs showed incomplete runs | `nohup` + `??` TTY daemon |
1064: | **Report hardcoded numbers** | Every results change needed manual LaTeX edits | Report showed different numbers than CSV | Use `\input{}` from auto-generated CSVs |
1065: | **33 stale sessions** | OpenCode DB 5.3 GB, no single source of truth | `du -sh ~/.local/share/opencode/` → 5.3GB | KleenHand process |
1066: 
1067: ### What Went Right
1068: 
1069: | Decision | Why It Helped |
1070: |---|---|
1071: | **Master sweep before fixing** | Found 18 bugs in one pass instead of 18 separate sessions |
1072: | **`opencode export <sessionID>`** | Extracted full session data as JSON — never lost |
1073: | **Hierarchical 3-level merge** | Each subagent handled 4-5 handoffs → context manageable → 2900-line ultimate handoff |
1074: | **Auto-generated LaTeX tables** | Report numbers always match CSV → one source of truth |
1075: | **Full config provenance per row** | Could filter by `k_inner=10` to get valid results, archive `k_inner=5` rows |
1076: | **`src frozen` before canonical** | Ensured all 540 rows used same code version |
1077: | **Evidence before claims** | Prevented overclaiming (lesson learned the hard way after 3 false fixes) |
1078: | **Tau ablation** | Directly answered "is tau the issue?" — yes, tau=100 was the entire "DRO fragile" narrative |
1079: | **Sequential canonical runner** | One writer, resume-safe, no collisions |
1080: | **Session handoff before delete** | Never lost a session's work even after deleting 33 sessions |
1081: 
1082: ### The Golden Rules (from real pain)
1083: 
1084: ```
1085: 1. COORDINATE before you run. One launcher. One writer per file. Kill by PID.
1086: 2. PROVENANCE every row. A result without its config is noise.
1087: 3. FREEZE src before canonical. Mixed code = mixed results = garbage.
1088: 4. NOHUP everything. If it takes >5 min, it must survive session death.
1089: 5. SWEEP don't guess. Run the numbers, show the output. "Should work" is not evidence.
1090: 6. AUTO-GENERATE tables. Hardcoded numbers in reports are ticking time bombs.
1091: 7. HANDOFF before delete. Extract first, delete second.
1092: 8. MERGE hierarchically. 3 levels. Never merge 29 handoffs at once.
1093: 9. DELETE empty sessions. 0-token sessions are just DB bloat.
1094: 10. ONE ultimate handoff. After KleenHand, only one file is the truth.
1095: ```

# KleenHand — Universal OpenCode Session Cleanup, Handoff Extraction & Project Completion Methodology

> **Author**: DRO-FairML session 2026-06-30 | **Version**: 2.0 — Universal
> **Purpose**: Reusable expert-level workflow to clean up any OpenCode project with 15+ stale sessions,
> extract handoffs, hierarchically merge, align misaligned agents, and drive to clean completion.
> **Status**: Battle-tested on 43-session DRO-FairML project. 33 stale sessions deleted. 1 ultimate handoff produced.

---

## TABLE OF CONTENTS
1. [Why This Is Needed](#1-why-this-is-needed)
2. [The Full Process (Flowchart)](#2-the-full-process-flowchart)
3. [Phase 0 — Parallel Project Status Sweep](#3-phase-0--parallel-project-status-sweep)
4. [Phase 1 — Session Cleanup](#4-phase-1--session-cleanup)
5. [Phase 2 — Handoff Extraction](#5-phase-2--handoff-extraction)
6. [Phase 3 — Hierarchical Merge](#6-phase-3--hierarchical-merge)
7. [Phase 4 — Project Completion](#7-phase-4--project-completion)
8. [Phase 5 — Agent Re-alignment Timeline](#8-phase-5--agent-re-alignment-timeline)
9. [Phase 6 — Deep Diagnostics & Self-Healing](#9-phase-6--deep-diagnostics--self-healing)
10. [Phase 7 — Git Hygiene & Audit](#10-phase-7--git-hygiene--audit)
11. [Phase 8 — Multi-Project Orchestration](#11-phase-8--multi-project-orchestration)
12. [Recommended Workflow Diagram](#12-recommended-workflow-diagram)
13. [Reusable Prompt Templates](#13-reusable-prompt-templates)
14. [Lessons Learned from DRO-FairML](#14-lessons-learned-from-dro-fairml)
15. [Quick Reference Card](#15-quick-reference-card)
16. [Final Words](#16-final-words)

---

## 1. Why This Is Needed

When you work on a project for weeks across **OpenCode CLI sessions**, you accumulate:

- **43+ sessions** with overlapping work, dead ends, and abandoned starts
- **No single source of truth** — knowledge scattered across sessions
- **Agent collision** — multiple agents writing the same files, using wrong configs
- **Session bloat** — OpenCode DB grows to 5+ GB with stale snapshots
- **Cannot delete sessions** without losing work → so nobody deletes them → DB keeps growing
- **No parallel awareness** — agents don't know what other agents are doing
- **No health monitoring** — experiments silently die, and nobody notices

**The KleenHand solution**: Ingest every session → extract handoffs → merge hierarchically via subagents → produce ONE ultimate handoff → delete all stale sessions → run deep diagnostics → continue with clean parallel-aware execution.

---

## 2. The Full Process (Flowchart)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                          KLEENHAND WORKFLOW v2 — UNIVERSAL                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                                  │
│  PHASE 0 ──► PARALLEL STATUS SWEEP                                              │
│  │            ├── git log --oneline -30 (all agents' work)                       │
│  │            ├── ps aux | grep python (all running experiments)                 │
│  │            ├── opencode session list (all stale sessions)                     │
│  │            ├── du -sh results/ logs/ (disk usage per area)                    │
│  │            ├── python3 -m pytest -q (test health)                             │
│  │            ├── ls -lt results/*.json (result freshness)                       │
│  │            └── git status --short (uncommitted delta)                         │
│  │                                                                               │
│  PHASE 1 ──► DELETE EMPTY SESSIONS (0 tokens) → opense session delete           │
│  │                                                                               │
│  PHASE 2 ──► EXPORT ALL → opencode export <id> → handoff_XXXX.md per session    │
│  │                                                                               │
│  PHASE 3 ──► HIERARCHICAL MERGE                                                 │
│  │            L1: Groups of 4-5 handoffs → merged_BATCH*.md                      │
│  │            L2: 2-3 batches → merged_L2*.md                                   │
│  │            L3: All L2 → ULTIMATE_HANDOFF.md                                  │
│  │                                                                               │
│  PHASE 4 ──► DELETE PROCESSED SESSIONS → clean temp files → FINAL_SPEC.md       │
│  │                                                                               │
│  PHASE 5 ──► AGENT RE-ALIGNMENT → identify collisions → canonical config →      │
│  │            freeze src → exclusive file ownership → rebuild                    │
│  │                                                                               │
│  PHASE 6 ──► DEEP DIAGNOSTICS → experiment health → disk pressure →             │
│  │            dependency audit → stale artifact scan → self-heal                 │
│  │                                                                               │
│  PHASE 7 ──► GIT HYGIENE → author audit → provenance trace →                    │
│  │            squash strategy → tag milestones                                   │
│  │                                                                               │
│  PHASE 8 ──► MULTI-PROJECT ORCHESTRATION → align all projects →                 │
│  │            common timeline → cross-project handoff                            │
│                                                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 3. Phase 0 — Parallel Project Status Sweep

Before ANY cleanup, run a **parallel status sweep** to snapshot the entire project state. This gives you the full picture before you start deleting anything.

### 3.1 The Master Status Dump (run ALL in parallel)

```bash
# ===== PARALLEL STATUS SWEEP — run all at once =====

echo "=== GIT LOG (last 30) ===" && git log --oneline -30
echo "=== GIT STATUS ===" && git status --short
echo "=== GIT DIFF STAT ===" && git diff --stat

echo "=== RUNNING PROCESSES ===" && ps aux | grep python | grep -v grep

echo "=== OPENCODE SESSIONS ===" && opencode session list

echo "=== RESULT FILES (freshness) ===" && ls -lt results/*.json 2>/dev/null | head -20

echo "=== DISK USAGE BY AREA ===" && du -sh results/ logs/ figures/ src/ data/ 2>/dev/null

echo "=== TEST HEALTH ===" && python3 -m pytest tests/ -q 2>&1

echo "=== CANONICAL PROGRESS ===" && python3 -c "
import json, glob, os
for f in sorted(glob.glob('results/*.json')):
    try:
        d = json.load(open(f))
        n = len(d) if isinstance(d, list) else len(d.keys())
        print(f'  {os.path.basename(f)}: {n} rows')
    except: print(f'  {os.path.basename(f)}: ERROR reading')
"
```

### 3.2 What Each Check Tells You

| Check | What It Reveals |
|---|---|
| `git log` | Which agents worked, what order, what's committed |
| `git status` | Uncommitted work, files modified by different agents |
| `ps aux` | Background experiments, their PIDs, CPU usage, runtime |
| `opencode session list` | How many stale sessions, their titles, last activity |
| `ls -lt results/*.json` | Which results are fresh vs stale, last modified time |
| `du -sh` | Disk pressure, unexpected bloat (e.g., 5GB OpenCode DB) |
| `pytest` | Whether codebase is healthy BEFORE cleanup |
| `du -sh ~/.local/share/opencode/` | OpenCode DB size — indicator of session bloat |

### 3.3 Snapshot for the Handoff

Save this entire sweep output into the ultimate handoff. The next agent should never have to re-discover this state.

### 3.4 Parallel Monitoring (watch multiple things at once)

```bash
# Monitor experiments + results + disk in parallel
watch -n 60 '
  echo "=== PROCESSES ==="
  ps aux | grep python | grep -v grep
  echo "=== CANONICAL ==="
  python3 -c "import json; print(len(json.load(open(\"results/canonical_tau1.json\"))))" 2>/dev/null || echo "no file"
  echo "=== DISK ==="
  du -sh ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db 2>/dev/null
  echo "=== GIT ==="
  git log --oneline -3
'
```

---

## 4. Phase 1 — Session Cleanup

### 4.1 List and categorize ALL sessions

```bash
# Full session dump with metadata
sqlite3 -column -header ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db "
SELECT s.id,
       substr(s.title,1,50) as title,
       datetime(s.time_created/1000,'unixepoch') as created,
       s.agent,
       s.tokens_input,
       s.tokens_output,
       s.cost,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM session_message m WHERE m.session_id=s.id) as msgs
FROM session s
WHERE s.project_id = (SELECT id FROM project WHERE worktree LIKE '%<PROJECT_DIR>%')
ORDER BY s.time_created;
"
```

### 4.2 Categorize sessions

| Category | Signal | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **Empty/abandoned** | `tokens_input = 0` | Delete immediately — no handoff needed |
| **Subagent sessions** | agent = "general" or title starts with "Agent" | Quick handoff — they did one specific task |
| **Main work sessions** | High tokens_input, meaningful title | Full handoff — core project work |
| **Current session** | The one you're in | Keep until done, then delete self last |
| **Duplicates** | Same title, same date range, one has content | Keep the one with content, delete the other |

### 4.3 Structured approach

```bash
# Step 1: Get all session IDs for this project
PROJECT_ID=$(sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db \
  "SELECT id FROM project WHERE worktree LIKE '%DRO-FairML%'")

# Step 2: Export all non-empty sessions
mkdir -p /tmp/session_exports
sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db \
  "SELECT id FROM session WHERE project_id='$PROJECT_ID' AND tokens_input > 0" \
  | while read sid; do
    opencode export "$sid" > "/tmp/session_exports/${sid}.json" 2>/dev/null &
    # Limit to 4 parallel exports
    while [ "$(jobs -r | wc -l)" -ge 4 ]; do sleep 1; done
  done
wait

# Step 3: Delete empty sessions (0 tokens)
sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db \
  "SELECT id FROM session WHERE project_id='$PROJECT_ID' AND tokens_input = 0" \
  | while read sid; do
    opencode session delete "$sid" 2>/dev/null
  done

# Step 4: Delete processed sessions after handoffs extracted
opencode session delete "<sessionID>"
```

---

## 5. Phase 2 — Handoff Extraction

### 5.1 From exported JSON, extract key data per session

Each export has this structure:
```json
{
  "info": {
    "id": "ses_...",
    "title": "...",
    "agent": "build",
    "model": {"id": "...", "providerID": "..."},
    "tokens": {"input": N, "output": N},
    "time": {"created": timestamp_ms, "updated": timestamp_ms},
    "summary": {"additions": N, "deletions": N, "files": N, "diffs": "..."},
    "cost": N
  },
  "messages": [
    {
      "info": {"role": "user", "agent": "build"},
      "parts": [{"type": "text", "text": "..."}]
    },
    {
      "info": {"role": "assistant"},
      "parts": [{"type": "reasoning", "text": "..."}, {"type": "text", "text": "..."}]
    }
  ]
}
```

### 5.2 Python extraction script

```python
import json, os, glob

exports = glob.glob("/tmp/session_exports/*.json")
for fpath in sorted(exports):
    sid = os.path.basename(fpath).replace(".json", "")
    d = json.load(open(fpath))
    info = d["info"]
    msgs = d.get("messages", [])

    # Get first user prompt
    first_prompt = ""
    for m in msgs:
        if m.get("info", {}).get("role") == "user":
            for p in m.get("parts", []):
                if p.get("type") == "text":
                    first_prompt = p.get("text", "")
                    break
            if first_prompt:
                break

    # Count tool calls
    tool_calls = sum(1 for m in msgs for p in m.get("parts", [])
                     if p.get("type") in ("bash", "write", "edit", "read", "grep", "glob"))

    # Generate handoff file
    handoff = f"""# Handoff {sid[:8]}
...
"""
    with open(f"handoff_{sid[:8]}.md", "w") as f:
        f.write(handoff)
```

### 5.3 The handoff_XXXX.md format

Every handoff file must contain:

```markdown
# Handoff XXXX

## Session identity
- **Tool**: opencode
- **Session ID**: `ses_...`
- **Title**: Exact session title
- **Agent**: build | general | plan
- **Model**: model ID used
- **Created**: date
- **Updated**: last active
- **Tokens**: X in / Y out
- **Messages**: N | **Tool calls**: M
- **Cost**: $

## What this session worked on
[The FULL first user prompt — this is the task that was given]

## What was accomplished
[Specific deliverables: files edited, results produced, commits made]

## Current state left behind
- Running processes (PIDs)
- Uncommitted changes
- Known issues or blockers

## Key files touched
[Every file this session edited or created — full paths]

## Handoff evidence
- Last commit hash:
- Test status (if applicable):
- Results files:
- Config parameters used:
```

---

## 6. Phase 3 — Hierarchical Merge

### 6.1 The 3-Level Merge Architecture

```
Level 1 (L1): Batch merge — 4-5 handoffs → 1 merged_BATCH file
Level 2 (L2): Intermediate merge — 2-3 BATCH files → 1 merged_L2 file
Level 3 (L3): ULTIMATE merge — 2 L2 files → ULTIMATE_HANDOFF.md

Why 3 levels?
- Each L1 subagent handles 4-5 handoffs → context window is comfortable
- Each L2 subagent handles broader themes → cross-batch patterns emerge
- L3 merges the two L2s → final document is exhaustive
- If you merge 29 handoffs in one shot → context blows up, details lost
```

### 6.2 Level 1: Batch (4-5 handoffs each)

```
BATCH 1: handoff_0000 + 0001 + 0002 + 0003 + 0004
BATCH 2: handoff_0005 + 0006 + 0007 + 0008 + 0009
BATCH 3: handoff_0010 + 0011 + 0012 + 0013 + 0014
BATCH 4: handoff_0015 + 0016 + 0017 + 0018 + 0019
BATCH 5: handoff_0020 + 0021 + A_experiments + B_code + C_analysis
BATCH 6: handoff_D_docs + A2 + C2 + D2
```

### 6.3 Level 2: Intermediate (2-3 batches each)

```
L2A: BATCH 1 + 2 + 3  (session exports — the historical record)
L2B: BATCH 4 + 5 + 6  (agent handoffs + final status)
```

### 6.4 Level 3: ULTIMATE

```
ULTIMATE: L2A + L2B
```

### 6.5 Typical output sizes (from DRO-FairML)

| Merge Level | Input | Output Lines | Compression |
|---|---|---|---|
| Level 1 (×6) | 5 handoffs each | 150-550 lines | 1.0× (all data) |
| Level 2 (×2) | 3 batches each | 1000-1250 lines | 1.0× (all data) |
| Level 3 (×1) | 2 L2s | 2900+ lines | 1.0×+ (all data + structure) |

### 6.6 Patch-based merge for huge projects

If you have 100+ handoffs (not 29), use patch-based merging:

```bash
# Instead of one big merge, do parallel sub-batches
# Sub-batch A: handoff_0000-0019 → merged_SA.md
# Sub-batch B: handoff_0020-0039 → merged_SB.md
# Sub-batch C: handoff_0040-0059 → merged_SC.md
# Sub-batch D: handoff_0060-0079 → merged_SD.md
# Sub-batch E: handoff_0080-0099 → merged_SE.md

# Then L2: SA+SB+SC → merged_L2A.md, SD+SE → merged_L2B.md
# Then L3: L2A+L2B → ULTIMATE_HANDOFF.md
```

This scales linearly. For 200 handoffs: 40 L1 merges → 8 L2 merges → 3 L3 merges → 1 final.

---

## 7. Phase 4 — Project Completion

### 7.1 Identify running experiments

```bash
ps aux | grep python | grep -v grep

# For each process, check:
# - PID
# - How long has it been running? (ELAPSED column in ps)
# - Is it making progress? (check output file timestamps)
# - Is it detached? (TTY=?? means survives session death)
```

### 7.2 Create FINAL_SPEC.md

Every FINAL_SPEC.md must have:

```markdown
# FINAL_SPEC — <Project Name>

## §0. CURRENT STATE
- Running PIDs, progress %, ETA
- Data completeness (X/N rows per dataset)
- Test status
- Code freeze status
- Blocked items

## §1. IMMEDIATE — DO NOT TOUCH
- Which processes are running and must not be interrupted
- Which files are being written

## §2. AFTER EXPERIMENTS — EXACT COMMAND SEQUENCE
- Step-by-step commands to regenerate everything
- Order matters (analysis → figures → PDFs → commit)

## §3. STALE CONTENT TO FIX
- Report/paper tables that need updating
- Hardcoded numbers vs auto-generated includes

## §4. BLOCKED ITEMS
- What's blocked, why, unblock strategy

## §5. FINAL DELIVERABLES CHECKLIST
- [ ] checkpoint items with row counts

## §6. COMMIT STRATEGY
- Which files to commit when, exact git commands

## §7. NARRATIVE SUMMARY
- One-paragraph for stakeholders (what was found, what's done, what's remaining)
```

### 7.3 Run everything that can run NOW

```bash
# Analysis (safe to run with partial data)
python3 experiments/compute_canonical_wilcoxon.py
python3 experiments/analyze_tau1.py
python3 experiments/generate_report_tables.py

# PDFs
tectonic --outdir report report/report.tex
tectonic --outdir paper paper/main.tex

# Figures
python3 experiments/generate_final_figures.py

# Tests
python3 -m pytest tests/ -q
```

### 7.4 Ensure process durability

```bash
# Check TTY column — ?? means daemon, s000 means terminal-attached
ps -o pid,tty,command -p <PID>

# If attached (TTY=s000 or similar), restart with nohup:
kill <PID>
nohup python3 -u experiments/run_canonical.py > logs/canonical_resume.log 2>&1 &

# Verify daemon
ps -o pid,tty,command -p $!
# Should show ?? in TTY column
```

### 7.5 Recovery commands (paste these into FINAL_SPEC.md)

```bash
# If processes die, restart with:
cd /path/to/project
nohup python3 -u experiments/run_canonical.py > logs/canonical_resume.log 2>&1 &
nohup python3 -u experiments/run_canonical_empirical.py > logs/empirical_resume.log 2>&1 &

# Monitor progress:
python3 -c "import json; print(len(json.load(open('results/canonical_tau1.json'))))"
python3 -c "import json; print(len(json.load(open('results/canonical_tau1_empirical.json'))))"
```

---

## 8. Phase 5 — Agent Re-alignment Timeline

### 8.1 The Problem

- **Agent A** used `K_inner=5` while **Agent B** used `K_inner=10` → results contaminated
- **Agent C** wrote to same JSON as **Agent A** → file lock contention → results frozen at 109/270
- **Agent D** referenced tau=100 data while everyone else moved to tau=1 → report stale
- **No provenance** on result rows → cannot tell which config produced which row

### 8.2 The Fix: Coordination Protocol

This protocol is **mandatory** for any multi-agent project. Print it, paste it, enforce it.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              COORDINATION PROTOCOL (NON-NEGOTIABLE)          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                              │
│  RULE 1: ONE agent launches ALL experiments.                 │
│          Others NEVER run anything remotely train-like.      │
│          "Agent A" is the sole runner.                       │
│                                                              │
│  RULE 2: ONE writer per results file.                       │

### 8.5 Detecting Agent Drift

Watch for these signals:

| Signal | What It Means | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `git log` shows same file edited by different agents | Ownership violation | Revert one, reassign |
| Results JSON has inconsistent keys | Different code versions wrote results | Re-run with frozen src |
| Report says one number, CSV says another | Hardcoded stale number | Replace with `\input{}` |
| Test count changes between sessions | Code changed without test update | Run tests, fix coverage |
| PIDs from days ago still running | Process was lost/timed out | Kill, restart with nohup |
| OpenCode DB >2 GB | Session bloat | Run KleenHand |

### 9.3 Common Failure Patterns & Self-Heal

| Pattern | Detection | Self-Heal |
|---|---|---|
| **Process hung** | CPU=0%, no file update >30min | `kill -9 <PID>` → restart with nohup |
| **JSON corruption** | JSON parse error in results file | Script should catch+skip bad entries, or restore from backup |
| **Out of disk** | `df -h` shows >90% | Find+delete caches, old snapshots, unused results |
| **Process killed by OOM** | Log ends with "Killed" or no error | Reduce memory (batch size, smaller model), or add swap |
| **Results file locked** | `write` tool fails | Kill other processes writing same file, restart single writer |
| **Session timeout** | Process dies when tool session ends | Use `nohup` + `??` TTY daemon |
| **Mixed configs** | Rows in same JSON have different `k_inner` | Add provenance field, filter by config for analysis |
| **Dependency drift** | ImportError after agent adds package | Use `requirements.txt`, freeze before canonical |

### 9.4 Self-Healing Commands

```bash
# Heal a hung process
kill -9 <PID> 2>/dev/null
nohup python3 -u experiments/run_canonical.py > logs/canonical_resume.log 2>&1 &
disown

# Heal a corrupted JSON
python3 -c "
import json
try:
    d = json.load(open('results/canonical_tau1.json'))
    print(f'OK: {len(d)} rows')
except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
    print(f'CORRUPTED at {e.pos}')
    # The last write was partial — truncate to last valid entry
    with open('results/canonical_tau1.json') as f:
        content = f.read()
    # Find last complete JSON object/array
    last_brace = content.rfind(']}')
    if last_brace > 0:
        content = content[:last_brace+2]
        with open('results/canonical_tau1.json', 'w') as f:
            f.write(content)
        d = json.load(open('results/canonical_tau1.json'))
        print(f'HEALED: {len(d)} rows')
"

# Heal orphaned lock files
find . -name "*.lock" -delete
find . -name "*.LCK" -delete

# Heal stale PID references
ps aux | grep defunct | grep -v grep  # Zombie processes
```

## 14. Lessons Learned from DRO-FairML

### What Went Wrong (so you don't repeat it)

| Problem | Impact | How Detected | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| **No coordination protocol** | 4 agents wrote same JSON → file frozen at 109/270 | `ls -lt` showed file unchanged for days | MASTER_PLAN §1 protocol |
| **K_inner=5 vs K_inner=10** | Results silently wrong for weeks | Brute-force audit found 18 bugs | Every row MUST record its config |
| **tau=100 vs tau=1** | "DRO is fragile" was actually tau artifact | Tau ablation sweep showed tau=1 fixes everything | Always sweep before concluding |
| **Oracle leak** | DRO knew real corruption rates | Code review: `corrupt_mask` passed to DRO | DRO knows only α, not mask |
| **pkill python** | Killed ALL 4 agents at once | All processes died simultaneously | Kill by PID only |
| **No background durability** | 270-run re-run died 8 times (timeouts, Terminated:15) | Logs showed incomplete runs | `nohup` + `??` TTY daemon |
| **Report hardcoded numbers** | Every results change needed manual LaTeX edits | Report showed different numbers than CSV | Use `\input{}` from auto-generated CSVs |
| **33 stale sessions** | OpenCode DB 5.3 GB, no single source of truth | `du -sh ~/.local/share/opencode/` → 5.3GB | KleenHand process |

### What Went Right

| Decision | Why It Helped |
|---|---|
| **Master sweep before fixing** | Found 18 bugs in one pass instead of 18 separate sessions |
| **`opencode export <sessionID>`** | Extracted full session data as JSON — never lost |
| **Hierarchical 3-level merge** | Each subagent handled 4-5 handoffs → context manageable → 2900-line ultimate handoff |
| **Auto-generated LaTeX tables** | Report numbers always match CSV → one source of truth |
| **Full config provenance per row** | Could filter by `k_inner=10` to get valid results, archive `k_inner=5` rows |
| **`src frozen` before canonical** | Ensured all 540 rows used same code version |
| **Evidence before claims** | Prevented overclaiming (lesson learned the hard way after 3 false fixes) |
| **Tau ablation** | Directly answered "is tau the issue?" — yes, tau=100 was the entire "DRO fragile" narrative |
| **Sequential canonical runner** | One writer, resume-safe, no collisions |
| **Session handoff before delete** | Never lost a session's work even after deleting 33 sessions |

### The Golden Rules (from real pain)

```
1. COORDINATE before you run. One launcher. One writer per file. Kill by PID.
2. PROVENANCE every row. A result without its config is noise.
3. FREEZE src before canonical. Mixed code = mixed results = garbage.
4. NOHUP everything. If it takes >5 min, it must survive session death.
5. SWEEP don't guess. Run the numbers, show the output. "Should work" is not evidence.
6. AUTO-GENERATE tables. Hardcoded numbers in reports are ticking time bombs.
7. HANDOFF before delete. Extract first, delete second.
8. MERGE hierarchically. 3 levels. Never merge 29 handoffs at once.
9. DELETE empty sessions. 0-token sessions are just DB bloat.
10. ONE ultimate handoff. After KleenHand, only one file is the truth.
```

1203: ## 16. Phase 9 — Autonomous Execution & Self-Optimizing Engine
1204: 
1205: ### 16.1 Why This Exists
1206: 
1207: The previous 8 phases require you to _run_ them. But what if KleenHand could **run itself**? This phase makes the process autonomous — it detects the project state, chooses the right path, executes, adapts, and even updates this document with lessons learned.
1208: 
1209: **Goal**: One agent invocation that does everything — status sweep → cleanup → handoff → merge → complete — without handholding.
1210: 
1211: ### 16.2 The Autonomous Orchestrator Prompt

1220: 
1221: ## MANDATORY EXECUTION ORDER

1502: ### 16.8 Autonomous Agent Swarm Pattern

1506: ```
1507: ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
1508: │                    AUTONOMOUS AGENT SWARM                              │

1515: │  ├── Spawns specialist agents                                         │
1516: │  └── Monitors all, consolidates results                               │
1517: │                                                                        │
1518: │  ├── MONITOR AGENT (1 per experiment PID)                             │
1519: │  │   ├── Every 5 min: check PID exists, CPU>0, file growing          │
1520: │  │   ├── If stalled: kill and restart with nohup                      │
1521: │  │   └── When done: signal orchestrator                               │
1522: │                                                                        │

1549: ### 16.9 Self-Healing Decision Table
1550: 
1551: When something goes wrong, the swarm must self-heal without human intervention:
1552: 
1553: | Failure | Detect | Self-Heal | Escalate If |
1554: |---|---|---|---|
1555: | Process hung (CPU=0, no file update) | `ps` shows PID, CPU=0, file mtime >30min | `kill -9 PID` → `nohup restart` | Fails 3× → document and continue |
1556: | JSON corrupted | `json.load()` raises `JSONDecodeError` | Truncate to last valid entry | Parse error persists after truncation |
1557: | Disk full | `df -h` shows >95% | Delete stale results, caches, old handoffs | <5% free after cleanup |
1558: | Session export fails | `opencode export` returns error | Skip and try next session, log failure | >10% of exports fail |
1559: | Merge produces small file | `wc -l < 100` | Re-merge with stricter "NO SUMMARIZE" prompt | Still small after 3 attempts |
1560: | PDF build fails | `tectonic` exit code != 0 | Check logs for error, fix common issues (fonts, packages) | Error requires human expertise |
1561: | Test fails | `pytest` exit code != 0 | Log which tests fail, check if pre-existing | New failures from code changes |
1562: | Process dies silently | PID gone, result file incomplete | Restart with resume: `nohup python3 ...` | No resume support in script |

1680: ### 17.2 What Each Pattern Means for KleenHand
1681: 
1682: #### 17.2.1 A2A Handoff Contract → Structured Handoff Schema
1683: 
1684: **External**: The A2A protocol defines agent-to-agent communication via JSON-RPC 2.0. The Agent Handoff Protocol adds 6 required fields: `trigger`, `source`, `target`, `context payload`, `acceptance criteria`, `recovery`.
1685: 
1686: **KleenHand addition**: Replace the freeform handoff_XXXX.md format with a **structured schema**:
1687: 
1688: ```yaml

1690: handoff:
1691:   version: "1.0"
1692:   id: "HANDOFF-20260630-0001"
1693:   trigger:
1694:     type: "session_termination"
1695:     reason: "cleanup_complete"
1696:   source:
1697:     agent_id: "ses_0e970c9a2ffe"
1698:     agent_type: "opencode/build"
1699:     last_commit: "3c0bcfc"
1700:     model: "deepseek-v4-flash-free"
1701:   target:
1702:     agent_id: "next_agent"
1703:     agent_type: "any"
1704:     required_capabilities: ["experiments", "analysis", "report"]
1705:   context:
1706:     payload_schema: "markdown"
1707:     includes:
1708:       - "Session identity and metadata"
1709:       - "First user prompt (the task)"
1710:       - "What was accomplished"
1711:       - "Current state (PIDs, progress, blockers)"
1712:       - "Key files touched"
1713:       - "Handoff evidence (commits, tests, results)"
1714:     provenance:
1715:       - source: "opencode export"
1716:         command: "opencode export <sessionID>"
1717:   acceptance_criteria:
1718:     - "All handoff fields populated"
1719:     - "Session ID matches a real OpenCode session"
1720:     - "PIDs verified against ps aux"
1721:   recovery:
1722:     on_failure: "Re-export session and regenerate handoff"
1723:     max_retries: 3
1724:     fallback: "Skip session, log as BLACK_HOLE"
1725: ```
1726: 
1727: **Benefit**: Machine-readable handoffs. Can be validated, grepped, and processed by automated tooling.
1728: 
1729: #### 17.2.2 Router Pattern → Session Classifier Agent
1730: 
1731: **External**: The router pattern (LangChain, Google Cloud) uses a classification step to route input to the right specialist agent.
1732: 
1733: **KleenHand addition**: Before Phase 1 (cleanup), add a **Router Agent** that classifies each session:
1734: 
1735: ```
1736: Session Classifier Router:
1737:   1. Read session title + tokens_input + first prompt
1738:   2. Classify as:
1739:      - EMPTY (0 tokens) → delete
1740:      - SUBAGENT (agent=general, short) → quick handoff
1741:      - MAIN_WORK (high tokens, meaningful title) → full handoff
1742:      - ORCHESTRATOR (manages other agents) → extract coordination decisions
1743:      - BLACK_HOLE (corrupted export, no data) → log and skip
1744:   3. Route to appropriate handoff template
1745:   4. Return routing decision for each session
1746: ```
1747: 
1748: **Benefit**: Handles 100 sessions as easily as 30. The router parallelizes classification.

1750: #### 17.2.3 Critic/Verifier Loop → Handoff Quality Gate
1751: 
1752: **External**: The critic pattern (IEEE CAI 2026, AutoCodeAI) adds a verifier agent that reviews output before it's accepted.

1754: **KleenHand addition**: After each handoff_XXXX.md is written, run a **Critic Agent** that validates:

1761:     - "Accomplishments are specific (not vague)"
1762:     - "PIDs are included if processes were running"
1763:     - "Files touched lists at least one file path"
1764:     - "Token counts match the export data"
1765:   pass_threshold: 4/6
1766:   on_fail: "Regenerate handoff with missing fields"
1767: ```

1769: **Benefit**: No more handoffs that say "did some work" with no specifics. Every handoff passes quality.

1771: #### 17.2.4 Git Worktree Isolation → Parallel Agent Workspaces
1772: 
1773: **External**: AgentWrapper (7.7K★) uses git worktrees so each parallel agent gets its own isolated branch + filesystem. ClawTeam (5.3K★) does the same.

1794: #### 17.2.5 Goal-Driven Decomposition → Self-Planning Orchestrator

## 16. Phase 9 — Autonomous Execution & Self-Optimizing Engine

### 16.1 Why This Exists

The previous 8 phases require you to _run_ them. But what if KleenHand could **run itself**? This phase makes the process autonomous — it detects the project state, chooses the right path, executes, adapts, and even updates this document with lessons learned.

**Goal**: One agent invocation that does everything — status sweep → cleanup → handoff → merge → complete — without handholding.

### 16.2 The Autonomous Orchestrator Prompt

This is the MASTER prompt. Feed it to a single high-level agent. It will orchestrate everything below.

```markdown
You are the KLEENHAND AUTONOMOUS ORCHESTRATOR.

Your mission: Take this project from whatever state it is in to clean completion.
You have full autonomy to read, analyze, execute, and adapt.

## MANDATORY EXECUTION ORDER

### STEP 1 — PARALLEL STATUS SWEEP
Run ALL of these in parallel:
- git log --oneline -30
- git status --short
- ps aux | grep python | grep -v grep
- opencode session list
- ls -lt results/*.json 2>/dev/null | head -20
- du -sh results/ logs/ figures/ src/ 2>/dev/null
- python3 -m pytest tests/ -q 2>&1
- python3 -c "import json,glob; [print(f'{f}: {len(json.load(open(f)))} rows') for f in sorted(glob.glob('results/*.json'))]"
- du -sh ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db 2>/dev/null

From the sweep, determine: Which phase is the project in?

### STEP 2 — ROUTE TO CORRECT PHASE
Use the routing table below. Execute ALL commands in the chosen phase.

### STEP 3 — QUALITY GATE
After each phase, verify the gate condition. If failed → diagnose and retry or skip.

### STEP 4 — RECURSIVE HANDOFF
After completing everything, append a "LESSON LEARNED" block to this document
(KleenHand.md) with:
- What worked well
- What this project uniquely needed
- What KleenHand was missing and should add
- The exact completion status

### STEP 5 — FINAL SUMMARY
Print a one-paragraph summary: what was accomplished, what's still running (PIDs),
and the exact command for the next agent to continue.

## ROUTING TABLE

| If state looks like... | Route to... |
|---|---|
| 15+ sessions with content, no handoffs exist | Phase 2 (Handoff Extraction) |
| Handoffs exist but not merged | Phase 3 (Hierarchical Merge) |
| ULTIMATE_HANDOFF.md exists, experiments running | Phase 4 (Project Completion) |
| Contaminated results, mixed configs | Phase 5 (Agent Re-alignment) |
| Only health check needed | Phase 6 (Deep Diagnostics) |
| Messy git history | Phase 7 (Git Hygiene) |
| Multiple projects | Phase 8 (Multi-Project) |

## TRANSITION RULES
- Always run Phase 0 first (status sweep) — no exceptions
- Run phases sequentially — never skip a phase
- After each phase, run the QUALITY GATE before moving on
- If a gate fails → diagnose, log the issue, attempt self-heal, retry
- If self-heal fails 3 times → document as BLOCKED and skip to next phase
- After ULTIMATE_HANDOFF.md is created, DELETE all handoff_*.md and merged_* files
- After all phases complete, write completion block to KleenHand.md itself
```

### 16.5 Dynamic Timeline & ETA Calculation

Instead of guessing ETA, **measure and extrapolate**:

```bash
# Measure actual progress rate
python3 -c "
import json, time, os

# Get current count
d = json.load(open('results/canonical_tau1.json'))
current = len(d)
target = 540

# Get file modification time
mtime = os.path.getmtime('results/canonical_tau1.json')
age_min = (time.time() - mtime) / 60

# Get rate from last N rows (check how fast rows are being added)
# If we know when the process started:
import subprocess
ps_out = subprocess.run(['ps', '-o', 'etime=,pid=', '-p', '6431'],
                       capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
# ps etime format: [[DD-]HH:]MM:SS
print(f'Process age: {ps_out}')
print(f'Current rows: {current}/{target}')
print(f'File age: {age_min:.0f} minutes')
print(f'Rate: {current/max(age_min,1):.2f} rows/min')
remaining = target - current
rate = current / max(age_min, 1)
if rate > 0:
    eta_min = remaining / rate
    print(f'ETA: {eta_min:.0f} minutes ({eta_min/60:.1f} hours)')
"

# Adaptive timeline — updates every poll
# If rate drops → flag for investigation
# If rate increases → update ETA

### 16.6 Adaptive Branching

Not all projects follow the same path. The orchestrator must **adapt** based on real-time conditions:

```python
# Pseudo-code for the adaptive router
def route(project_state):
    if project_state["has_open_sessions"]:
        if project_state["empty_sessions"] > 0:
            run("Phase 1 — Delete empty sessions")
        if project_state["meaningful_sessions"] > 0:
            if not project_state["has_handoffs"]:
                run("Phase 2 — Extract handoffs")
            else:
                run("Phase 3 — Merge handoffs")

    if project_state["has_ultimate_handoff"]:
        if project_state["experiments_running"]:
            if project_state["has_partial_data"]:
                run("Phase 4 — Run analysis with partial data")
            run("Phase 4 — Monitor experiments")
        elif project_state["all_data_collected"]:
            run("Phase 4 — Full completion pipeline")
        else:
            run("Phase 4 — Launch experiments")

    if project_state["has_collisions"]:
        run("Phase 5 — Re-align agents")

    if project_state["needs_diagnostics"]:
        run("Phase 6 — Deep diagnostics")

    if project_state["git_dirty"]:
        run("Phase 7 — Git hygiene")

    if project_state["multiple_projects"]:
        run("Phase 8 — Multi-project orchestration")

    if project_state["all_gates_pass"]:
        mark_complete()
```

### 16.7 Recursive Self-Update Mechanism

This is the most powerful pattern: **KleenHand updates itself** after every run.

```markdown
## RECURSIVE SELF-UPDATE PROTOCOL

After every orchestration run, append a block to this file:

```

This means every project improves KleenHand. Over time, it becomes exponentially more robust.

The highest level of autonomy: instead of one orchestrator, spawn a **swarm of specialist agents** that each monitor and act independently.

### 16.9 Self-Healing Decision Table

When something goes wrong, the swarm must self-heal without human intervention:

| Failure | Detect | Self-Heal | Escalate If |
|---|---|---|---|
| Process hung (CPU=0, no file update) | `ps` shows PID, CPU=0, file mtime >30min | `kill -9 PID` → `nohup restart` | Fails 3× → document and continue |
| JSON corrupted | `json.load()` raises `JSONDecodeError` | Truncate to last valid entry | Parse error persists after truncation |
| Disk full | `df -h` shows >95% | Delete stale results, caches, old handoffs | <5% free after cleanup |
| Session export fails | `opencode export` returns error | Skip and try next session, log failure | >10% of exports fail |
| Merge produces small file | `wc -l < 100` | Re-merge with stricter "NO SUMMARIZE" prompt | Still small after 3 attempts |
| PDF build fails | `tectonic` exit code != 0 | Check logs for error, fix common issues (fonts, packages) | Error requires human expertise |
| Test fails | `pytest` exit code != 0 | Log which tests fail, check if pre-existing | New failures from code changes |
| Process dies silently | PID gone, result file incomplete | Restart with resume: `nohup python3 ...` | No resume support in script |

### 16.11 Bootstrap Command

The single command that starts everything:

```bash
# ONE COMMAND TO RULE THEM ALL
# Paste this into OpenCode CLI for ANY messy project:

opencode "
Run the full KleenHand autonomous orchestrator on this project.

1. Read ~/Desktop/KleenHand.md completely — section 16 (Autonomous Execution) is your bible.
2. Start with Phase 0 (Parallel Status Sweep) — run ALL commands in parallel.
3. Detect the current state from the state machine (§16.3).
4. Route to the correct phase using the routing table.
5. Execute each phase sequentially, running ALL commands within that phase.
6. After each phase, run the quality gate (§16.4). If it fails, self-heal and retry up to 3×.
7. After ALL phases complete, append an AUTO-APPENDED RUN LOG to KleenHand.md itself.
8. Print final summary with PIDs, row counts, and next action.

CRITICAL RULES:
- NO skipping phases. Always start with Phase 0.
- NO summarizing sweep output. Include ALL raw command outputs.
- NO deleting the current session until everything is done.
- Self-heal before escalating. If stuck after 3 retries, document and continue.
- Update KleenHand.md with lessons learned from THIS project.
"
```

This single prompt, combined with the KleenHand.md document, should be able to autonomous handle any OpenCode project.

## 17. Phase 10 — External Pattern Integration (from Internet Research 2026)

This section maps the **best external patterns** from the 2026 agentic AI ecosystem onto KleenHand.
Each recommendation is specific to the "cleanup → handoff → merge → complete" use case.

### 17.1 Research Sources Consulted

| Source | What Was Found |
|---|---|
| **Google A2A Protocol** (Linux Foundation) | Open standard for agent-to-agent communication; handoff contracts |
| **IEEE CAI 2026** | Multi-agent production patterns; fault tolerance; observability |
| **LangChain Blog** | 4 multi-agent patterns: subagent, skills, handoff, router |
| **Google Cloud Architecture** | Design pattern decision tree for agentic systems |
| **GitHub (7.7K★) AgentWrapper** | Parallel agent orchestrator with git worktrees + CI feedback |
| **GitHub (10.6K★) OpenHive** | Multi-agent harness with state persistence, crash recovery, self-healing |
| **GitHub (6.4K★) Open Multi-Agent** | Goal-driven coordinator → task DAG decomposition |
| **GitHub (5.3K★) ClawTeam** | Agent swarm intelligence; leader spawns workers via CLI |
| **GitHub Agent Kanban** | Agent-first board with cryptographic IDs, roles, skills |
| **Works With Agents Blog** | Agent handoff protocol standard proposal |
| **Microsoft ISE Blog** | A2A context-passing patterns (embedded, shared, per-agent) |
| **ECOA AI / Inventiple / VPSMAC** | Production multi-agent guides 2026 |

### 17.2 What Each Pattern Means for KleenHand

#### 17.2.1 A2A Handoff Contract → Structured Handoff Schema

**External**: The A2A protocol defines agent-to-agent communication via JSON-RPC 2.0. The Agent Handoff Protocol adds 6 required fields: `trigger`, `source`, `target`, `context payload`, `acceptance criteria`, `recovery`.

**KleenHand addition**: Replace the freeform handoff_XXXX.md format with a **structured schema**:

```yaml
# handoff_contract.yaml (future replacement for handoff_XXXX.md)
handoff:
  version: "1.0"
  id: "HANDOFF-20260630-0001"
  trigger:
    type: "session_termination"
    reason: "cleanup_complete"
  source:
    agent_id: "ses_0e970c9a2ffe"
    agent_type: "opencode/build"
    last_commit: "3c0bcfc"
    model: "deepseek-v4-flash-free"
  target:
    agent_id: "next_agent"
    agent_type: "any"
    required_capabilities: ["experiments", "analysis", "report"]
  context:
    payload_schema: "markdown"
    includes:
      - "Session identity and metadata"
      - "First user prompt (the task)"
      - "What was accomplished"
      - "Current state (PIDs, progress, blockers)"
      - "Key files touched"
      - "Handoff evidence (commits, tests, results)"
    provenance:
      - source: "opencode export"
        command: "opencode export <sessionID>"
  acceptance_criteria:
    - "All handoff fields populated"
    - "Session ID matches a real OpenCode session"
    - "PIDs verified against ps aux"
  recovery:
    on_failure: "Re-export session and regenerate handoff"
    max_retries: 3
    fallback: "Skip session, log as BLACK_HOLE"
```

**Benefit**: Machine-readable handoffs. Can be validated, grepped, and processed by automated tooling.

#### 17.2.2 Router Pattern → Session Classifier Agent

**External**: The router pattern (LangChain, Google Cloud) uses a classification step to route input to the right specialist agent.

**KleenHand addition**: Before Phase 1 (cleanup), add a **Router Agent** that classifies each session:

```
Session Classifier Router:
  1. Read session title + tokens_input + first prompt
  2. Classify as:
     - EMPTY (0 tokens) → delete
     - SUBAGENT (agent=general, short) → quick handoff
     - MAIN_WORK (high tokens, meaningful title) → full handoff
     - ORCHESTRATOR (manages other agents) → extract coordination decisions
     - BLACK_HOLE (corrupted export, no data) → log and skip
  3. Route to appropriate handoff template
  4. Return routing decision for each session
```

**Benefit**: Handles 100 sessions as easily as 30. The router parallelizes classification.

#### 17.2.3 Critic/Verifier Loop → Handoff Quality Gate

**External**: The critic pattern (IEEE CAI 2026, AutoCodeAI) adds a verifier agent that reviews output before it's accepted.

**KleenHand addition**: After each handoff_XXXX.md is written, run a **Critic Agent** that validates:

```yaml
handoff_quality_check:
  checks:
    - "Session ID is present and valid"
    - "First prompt is captured (not empty)"
    - "Accomplishments are specific (not vague)"
    - "PIDs are included if processes were running"
    - "Files touched lists at least one file path"
    - "Token counts match the export data"
  pass_threshold: 4/6
  on_fail: "Regenerate handoff with missing fields"
```

**Benefit**: No more handoffs that say "did some work" with no specifics. Every handoff passes quality.

#### 17.2.4 Git Worktree Isolation → Parallel Agent Workspaces

**External**: AgentWrapper (7.7K★) uses git worktrees so each parallel agent gets its own isolated branch + filesystem. ClawTeam (5.3K★) does the same.

**KleenHand addition**: For Phase 5 (agent re-alignment), use git worktrees:

```bash
# Each agent gets an isolated worktree
git worktree add ../DRO-FairML-agent-A lane-A
git worktree add ../DRO-FairML-agent-B lane-B
git worktree add ../DRO-FairML-agent-C lane-C
git worktree add ../DRO-FairML-agent-D lane-D

# Agent A works in lane-A, Agent B in lane-B, etc.
# No file collisions because each has their own checkout
# Results merged back to main via cherry-pick or merge

# After completion, prune worktrees
git worktree prune
```

**Benefit**: Eliminates the #1 problem (file collision) from the DRO-FairML project. Each agent literally cannot write to another agent's files.

#### 17.2.5 Goal-Driven Decomposition → Self-Planning Orchestrator

**External**: Open Multi-Agent (6.4K★) takes a goal and the coordinator decomposes it into a task DAG at runtime. No fixed phases.

**KleenHand addition**: Instead of hardcoded Phase 0→1→2→3, add a **Goal-Driven Mode**:

```markdown
## Goal-Driven Mode (alternative to fixed phases)

Instead of running phases sequentially, give the orchestrator ONE goal:

GOAL: "Clean this project, extract all session knowledge,
       merge into one handoff, and leave it ready for completion."

The orchestrator:
1. Reads the project state (Phase 0)
2. Decomposes the goal into tasks dynamically
3. Parallelizes independent tasks
4. Adapts the task graph based on what it finds
5. Only runs phases that are NEEDED
```

**Benefit**: If a project only has 5 sessions, it won't waste time on the full 8-phase pipeline. It self-sizes.

#### 17.2.6 State Persistence & Crash Recovery

**External**: OpenHive (10.6K★) persists agent state and can crash-recover any agent. Checkpoint-based recovery.

**KleenHand addition**: Add checkpoint files between phases:

```bash
# After each phase completes, write a checkpoint
echo "PHASE_0_COMPLETE" > .kleenhand_checkpoint
echo "PHASE_1_COMPLETE" >> .kleenhand_checkpoint
# etc.

# On restart, read checkpoints and skip completed phases
if grep -q "PHASE_2_COMPLETE" .kleenhand_checkpoint; then
  echo "Phase 2 already complete, skipping..."
fi
```

**Benefit**: If the orchestrator session dies mid-cleanup, it can resume from the last checkpoint instead of restarting from Phase 0.

#### 17.2.7 Agent Swarm Intelligence → Self-Organizing Subagents

**External**: ClawTeam (5.3K★) leader agent spawns worker agents that self-organize. Essaim adds behavior catalog + announcement protocol to prevent agent collision.

**KleenHand addition**: The Level-1 merge subagents should use an **announcement protocol**:

```markdown
## Agent Collision Prevention for Subagents

Before any subagent starts work, it MUST:
1. Announce intent: "I am working on merged_BATCH1.md"
2. Coordinate: check if another agent claimed the same batch
3. Stake claim: write a .lock file for the batch
4. Execute: do the merge
5. Release: remove .lock file

Lock file format: .lock_merged_BATCH1 → contains agent ID + start time
Stale lock timeout: 5 minutes (automatic release)
```

**Benefit**: Prevents two subagents from merging the same batch (the Level-1 equivalent of the K_inner=5 collision).

#### 17.2.8 Observability & Tracing

**External**: Every production multi-agent guide (IEEE CAI, ECOA AI, VPSMAC) insists on observability with OpenTelemetry correlation IDs across agent boundaries.

**KleenHand addition**: Add a tracing log that records every action:

```markdown
## Agent Trace Log

Every agent action is logged to .kleenhand_trace.jsonl:

{"ts": "2026-06-30T10:00:00Z", "agent": "orchestrator", "phase": 0, "action": "status_sweep", "result": "33 sessions found"}
{"ts": "2026-06-30T10:01:00Z", "agent": "orchestrator", "phase": 1, "action": "delete_empty", "result": "16 sessions deleted"}
{"ts": "2026-06-30T10:02:00Z", "agent": "router", "action": "classify", "result": "17 main_work, 5 subagent"}
{"ts": "2026-06-30T10:05:00Z", "agent": "handoff_extractor", "batch": 1, "action": "export", "session": "ses_1234", "result": "success"}
```

**Benefit**: When something goes wrong, you can trace exactly which agent did what, when.

### 17.3 Recommended Addition Priority

Based on what KleenHand is missing and what would give the most value:

| **P0** | Structured Handoff Schema (§17.2.1) | A2A / Handoff Protocol | Machine-readable handoffs, validation |

### 17.4 One-Line Verdict

From the entire internet research sweep for KleenHand:
